A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same entropy–memorization study despite the changed title and organization. The complete 26-page v3 and 33-page v4, including their appendices, provide sufficient readable text, equations, figures, and tables for comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original entropy–memorization regressions, sampling and continuation-length experiments, semantic-cluster analyses, and dataset-inference predictions.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds model evaluations, zlib comparisons, robustness analyses, and dataset-inference baseline comparisons.

M1.justification: The core level-set entropy estimator, entropy normalization, and intercept-based dataset-inference rule remain. v4 adds a set-level zlib procedure that compresses concatenated sequences and an optional coarse-score-binning variant (Section 3.2 and Appendix C.4). These are limited procedural extensions.

E1.justification: v4 adds RedPajama data for OpenLlama evaluations and explicitly evaluates the central relationship on Pile data with Pythia. Pile-derived MIMIR, Dolma, OLMo-2-Mix, and LiveBench already appeared in v3. The semantic domains are retained; additional model sizes and instruction tuning chiefly change experimental configurations.

E2.justification: v4 adds evaluated zlib alternatives at both instance and set levels, alongside the retained entropy approaches. Appendix E.2 also introduces Maini et al. (2024) as an actual dataset-inference comparator, reporting predictions and runtimes in Tables 6–7. v3 had no evaluated external dataset-inference baseline.

E3.justification: v4 introduces OpenLlama-7B/13B, Pythia-70M, and OLMo-2-Instruct configurations, coarse-binning and sample-size protocols, and a baseline comparison using equal evaluation-data amounts and common hardware for timing. The default 100-token prompt, 50-token continuation, edit-distance metric, and LCS filtering remain. The GPT-2-XL evaluation is removed.

E4.justification: New analyses test sensitivity to score-bin granularity (Appendix C.4), memorization after instruction tuning (C.6), and dataset-inference sample sizes from 250 to 8,000 (E.1). The last analysis supports the already-stated 1,500-sample minimum. Temperature, continuation-length, and 16-cluster analyses largely retain their earlier evidence.

E5.justification: Appendix E.2 newly specifies a p-value threshold of 0.05 for the Maini dataset-inference comparator, adding a significance-based membership decision procedure. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or cross-run variability for the entropy correlations and timing results.

E6.justification: v4 adds substantial results, including OpenLlama correlations of 0.956 (13B) and 0.814 (7B), robustness results, and Maini comparisons reporting 5/6 versus 3/6 correct predictions. The OLMo-2 normalized-entropy correlation changes from -0.816 to -0.906, and the stated perfect-memorization token count changes from 2^6 to 2^10 without an explained setting change. The GPT-2-XL/LiveBench row disappears. Core OLMo correlations and all 16 cluster regression plots are retained.

T1.justification: Equation 4 changes the empirical-probability denominator from N times sequence length to the score-group cardinality times sequence length, correcting the intended conditional normalization. However, v4 Algorithm 1 still uses N times sequence length. This is a substantive mathematical correction with an unresolved inconsistency; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central entropy–edit-distance relationship and dataset-inference application remain. v4 adds explicit model-agnostic and quantitative-compressibility contribution claims, promotes the normalized-entropy trend as a linear variant, and presents dataset inference as a secondary observation in the abstract. The expanded validation primarily supports the retained central claim.

C2.justification: v4 adds mechanisms involving token frequency, long-tailed natural language versus specialized text, and instruction tuning. It interprets the retained biomedical-cluster result as a domain-shift limitation, explains incompatibility with post-training dataset formats, and describes auditing with a known training subset. The lack of theoretical explanation remains acknowledged, partly relocated to the conclusion.

D1.justification: v4 adds baseline implementation information, including 16 aggregated metrics, training/validation sampling, single-A100-80GB-PCIe hardware, and timings. It removes v3's general four-RTX-3090, Ubuntu 22.04, and vLLM disclosure. These are mixed documentation changes; they do not establish that retained experiments were rerun on different hardware.

R1.justification: v4 substantially repositions the work around previous compressibility attempts and quantitative memorization research. It adds substantive comparisons with Prashanth et al. (2025), Zhou et al. (2024), and Morris et al. (2025), plus information-theory and influence-function context. This extends beyond bibliography updates or citation-style changes.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around compressibility. The first-attempt/second-attempt narrative becomes Preliminaries and Methodology, instance-wise implementation moves to Appendix B, and dataset inference is reorganized into several main-text subsections. Terminology, conclusions, appendix organization, and author/header presentation also change substantially.

P2.justification: v4 restructures the main figures into comparator panels, splits the normalized-entropy/token-count display, adds robustness plots and comparison tables, and redraws the clustering summary. Existing continuation-length and dataset-inference displays move into the main text, while v3's intercept–slope scatter disappears. The journal layout and table placement are extensively revised.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially addresses v3's narrow central validation and absence of evaluated external comparators through additional model/corpus evaluations, zlib comparisons, binning and sample-size checks, and a Maini dataset-inference benchmark. These materially strengthen the empirical support and clarify research positioning. The gains remain substantial despite unresolved formula/pseudocode and protocol-description inconsistencies, unexplained normalized-result changes, and the loss of general compute details.
